'''David Colin Hanna''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (10 April 1941<ref>{{cite LCAuth |id=n79092342}}</ref> − 27 January 2026<ref>{{cite web | title=In Memoriam: David C. Hanna, 1941-2026 | website=Optica | year=2026 | url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/obituaries/2026/david_c_hanna/ | access-date=2 March 2026}}</ref>) was a British [[physicist]] specializing in [[laser physics]] and [[nonlinear optics]]. He was emeritus professor of physics at the [[University of Southampton]]. His research interests include quasi-phase-matched nonlinear materials, optical parametric oscillators, fibre lasers, and X-ray sources based on high harmonic generation.<ref name="Ferguson">{{cite journal | first=A. I.| last=Ferguson| title=Honorary Editor's introduction | journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics | publisher=IOP Publishing | volume=34 | issue=16 | date=1 August 2001 | issn=0022-3727 | doi=10.1088/0022-3727/34/16/001 | page=34}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.phys.soton.ac.uk/staff/index.php?staff=dch |title=	David Hanna |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101221052340/http://www.phys.soton.ac.uk/staff/index.php?staff=dch |archive-date=December 21, 2010 |access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref>

Hanna was awarded the [[Max Born Prize]] in 1993,<ref name="IOP">{{cite web | title=Born medal recipients | website=Institute of Physics | url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/bilateral/born/medallists/page_38473.html | access-date=9 October 2018 | archive-date=16 March 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316061636/http://www.iop.org/about/awards/bilateral/born/medallists/page_38473.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[European Physical Society]] [[Prize for Applied Aspects of Quantum Electronics and Optics]] in 2000,<ref name="QEP">{{cite web | title=QEOD Prizes - EPS Quantum Electronics Prizes | website=European Physical Society (EPS) | date=1 August 2018 | url=https://www.eps.org/members/group_content_view.asp?group=85201&id=315903 | access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref> and the [[Charles Hard Townes Medal]] in 2003.<ref name=OSA>{{cite web| url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/charlestownes/| title=Charles Hard Townes Medal| website=The Optical Society| access-date=7 October 2018}}</ref> Hanna was elected to the [[Royal Society]] in 1998.<ref name="RS">{{cite web | title=David Hanna | website=Royal Society | year=2015 | url=https://royalsociety.org/people/david-hanna-11573/ | access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref>
